title: Math Quizz backup, format version 1
description: A full copy of ONE Math Quizz profile as exported from Settings → Tes données. Since 0.12.0 a device can hold several named profiles (siblings sharing a tablet); a backup covers exactly one of them and carries no list of the others, so importing a file never creates, renames or removes a profile — it writes into a destination the user picked, either replacing that profile's data or, since 1.2.0, merging the file's sessions into it. Math Quizz is a fully client-side app: this file is the only way its data ever leaves the browser. Everything here is written and read locally; there is no server and no account. Only `format`, `formatVersion` and `data` are required — a third party generating a file may omit any other field, and the app will fill in a sensible default. Any property present must have the type declared here: the importer rejects the whole file on a type error rather than silently dropping records.

$schema.description: URL of this schema. Written on export so an editor or a validator can pick it up automatically; ignored on import.

format.description: Fixed marker identifying the file as a Math Quizz backup. The importer rejects any other value as 'not a Math Quizz export'.

formatVersion.description: Version of THIS envelope format, not of the app. Bumped only on a breaking change to the shape below. The importer accepts version 1 and reports anything else as coming from a newer (or unknown) version.

exportedAt.description: When the file was written, ISO 8601 with milliseconds and a UTC 'Z' suffix. Informational: it dates the suggested filename and the import confirmation. Empty or absent is accepted.

appVersion.description: The package.json version of the app that produced the file (e.g. '0.10.0'). Informational only — compatibility is decided by formatVersion, never by this.

profile.description: Id of the profile the data belongs to — the segment in its localStorage prefix, 'mathquizz:profile:<id>:'. The profile that predates multiple profiles keeps the id 'default'; ones created since carry an opaque id. Informational only: the importer writes into the destination the user chose, never into the profile this names, because an id minted on another device may mean someone else here, or nobody.

profileName.description: Display name of that profile ('Léa'), or empty when it had none — the profile carried over from before 0.12.0 was never named. Informational: the app shows it in the import confirmation so the reader can tell whose file this is, and folds it into the suggested filename. Never used to pick or create a destination profile.

data.description: The profile payload — one property per localStorage key the app owns. Every property is optional; an absent one imports as empty (or, for settings, as the app defaults).

settings.description: The child's preferences, from 'mathquizz:profile:<id>:settings'. Unlike the rest of the file, settings are sanitised rather than rejected: an out-of-range number is clamped and an unknown enum value falls back to the app default, because every setting has a safe default.

history.description: Completed timed tests, oldest first, from 'mathquizz:profile:<id>:history'. The app keeps at most the 50 most recent; a longer array imports fine but is trimmed to the newest 50. A merge import trims the combined history the same way, so it can drop older sessions from either side.

trainingHistory.description: Completed training sessions (the mode that corrects each answer immediately), oldest first, from 'mathquizz:profile:<id>:training-history'. Same shape and same 50-entry cap as `history`; kept separate so training practice does not distort test scores.

errors.description: DEPRECATED since 0.11.0, and no longer written. Lifetime per-pair counters from 'mathquizz:profile:<id>:errors', as produced by versions up to 0.10.0. The app now derives every per-pair statistic from the histories and weights recent sessions more heavily, which a running total carrying no timestamps cannot express. A file carrying this section still validates and still imports: it is checked for shape, then dropped.

durationPerQuestionMs.description: Target answer time in milliseconds. Answering within it earns a full point; slower but correct earns partialCreditFactor. Clamped to 1000–60000 and rounded to a multiple of 10 on import, the finest step the timer shows.

questionCount.description: How many questions a session draws. Clamped to 1–200 on import.

selectedTables.description: Which multiplication tables the questions are drawn from. Values outside the app's table list are dropped; if nothing valid remains, the default selection is restored — an empty selection would make question generation fail.

mode.description: Which operations are asked: multiplication only, division only, or a mix.

answerMode.description: How answers are collected: 'screen' (on-screen numpad, timed), 'paper' (answers written on paper, self-marked afterwards), 'training' (immediate correction, untimed scoring), 'list' (a printable list of problems — a view, so it records no session).

partialCreditFactor.description: Points awarded for a correct answer given after the target time, from 0 (none) to 1 (as good as a fast answer). Clamped to 0–1 on import.

adaptiveDraw.description: How strongly the question draw favours pairs the child has recently been getting wrong: 'off' (every pair equally likely), 'moderate' or 'strong'. Absent in files written before the field existed — read an absent value as 'moderate'.

sessionResult.description: One completed session. The settings fields are copied in at the time the session ran, so a score can be re-derived exactly even after the child changes their settings.

id.description: Opaque random identifier, written when the session is recorded (since 1.2.0; the app uses 32 lowercase hex characters, but readers should treat it as any non-empty string). It is how a merge import recognises a session it already holds, even when two devices stamped the same startedAt. Sessions recorded by earlier versions have no id and never get one retroactively; a merge matches those on startedAt plus the number of answers instead. An id that is present but not a non-empty string makes the file corrupt. A writer creating new sessions should give each one a fresh id, and must not reuse one for a different session.

startedAt.description: When the session began, ISO 8601. The sort key: a merge import re-sorts both histories by it, so a device with a wrong clock files its sessions in the wrong place. For sessions without an id, it is also half of the key a merge matches on.

durationPerQuestionMs.description: The target time in force during this session.

partialCreditFactor.description: The partial-credit factor in force during this session.

questionCount.description: How many questions were requested. May exceed answers.length if the session was cut short.

selectedTables.description: The tables in play during this session.

mode.description: The operation mode in force during this session.

answerMode.description: How the answers were collected. Screen sessions recorded by versions up to 1.1.0 omit it, as does anything older than the field — read an absent value as 'screen'. Never 'list', which records no session. 'paper' only appears in histories written by versions up to 1.1.0: later versions never save a paper test, and the app leaves such sessions out of every statistic, because the child marked them against the answers shown on screen.

answers.description: One record per question actually presented, in the order asked.

given.description: What the child typed. null in paper records, where the app never sees the written answer. Histories written by older versions can also hold null in screen records, meaning time ran out with no answer; no current mode produces that, but readers should still count such a record as a timeout.

elapsedMs.description: Time taken to answer, in milliseconds. Compared against the session's durationPerQuestionMs to decide full or partial credit.

selfMarkedCorrect.description: Whether the answer counts as right, when present. It overrides the given/expected comparison for scoring and statistics. Paper records (written by versions up to 1.1.0 only): the child's own mark on the results screen, with `given` null because the app never sees what was written. Training records: the app's own check, stored next to the numeric `given` it was computed from. Screen records omit it.

question.description: A question is always stored as the pair (a, b) plus an operator, never as the rendered text. For 'mul' the child is shown 'a × b' and `expected` is a×b. For 'div' the child is shown '(a×b) ÷ a' and `expected` is b — so the same stored pair backs both directions, and both feed the same error counter. The app rejects the whole file on import if any question breaks the arithmetic rule for `expected`, which this schema cannot express on its own.

a.description: First operand: the table being drilled. A positive integer; the app currently offers 2–12, 15, 24 and 25, but older sessions may hold a table that has since been dropped, and they still import.

b.description: Second operand: the multiplier. A positive integer; currently 2–12, but 1 and 15 were multipliers before 2026-06-13 and sessions from then still import.

op.description: Which way the pair is asked.

expected.description: The correct answer: a×b for 'mul', b for 'div'. Enforced on import: any other value makes the file corrupt.

errorStats.description: Counters keyed by canonical pair. The key is '<low>x<high>' with the two operands sorted ascending (7×8 and 8×7 both key '7x8'), so multiplication and division of the same pair accumulate together. Keys that do not match that shape are rejected.

attempts.description: How many times the pair was presented. Every presentation counts here, right or wrong.

errors.description: How many of those attempts got a wrong answer (a subset of attempts).

timeouts.description: How many of those attempts got no answer before time ran out (a subset of attempts).
